example.title: Chicago and North Western Railroad Bridge over the Eagle River

brief: 337 ft single-track railway viaduct sitting about 10 ft above high water: three central riveted steel deck plate girder spans of about 65 ft each on massive cribbed timber piers (rows of 14x12 timbers under four courses of 12x12s), flanked by eleven timber pile-trestle approach spans of 10-13 ft (seven north, four south) on cross-braced 12 in pile bents with 13x13 caps and triple 16x8 stringers. Girders are plate-and-angle I-sections with stiffener angles and cross-frames between them. In railway service it carried open-deck ties with a riveted steel plate railing, later an open steel railing; the 1990s photos show it as a snowmobile trail with new plank deck and a two-course wooden rail, piers partly cased in concrete.

traits.deck: open ties on girders and timber stringers
